title: How TCP congestion control works
sub: A sender can't see the network, so it probes: double fast, then creep up, and halve the moment packets get dropped. Each step here is one round trip.
aria: A chart of the TCP congestion window per round trip against the bottleneck capacity line
breakLabel: 💥 Break it: the sender ignores loss and never backs off
breakOff: Normal run: TCP Reno-style. Slow start, then +1 per round trip, and halve on loss.
breakOn: The sender keeps growing its window no matter what. Past capacity the buffer overflows, dropped packets get resent, and useful throughput collapses.
learn: Slow start doubles the window every round trip, which is exponential, until it reaches the threshold. Then congestion avoidance adds one per round trip.
On loss the window is cut in half. The classic sawtooth is TCP probing for the capacity and backing off.
Raise the random loss slider: the connection never reaches capacity, because every loss halves the window.
Break it: with no backoff the link is overloaded, so goodput (useful data delivered) falls. Senders backing off is what stops the network from collapsing.
Simplified model: Reno-style, one step per round trip, and the collapse curve in Break it is illustrative, not measured.
